text:
Anthropic Skills just turned your best prompt into a file you can ship.

What changed: on August 19, Computer Use, the new Browser Use tool, the Skills API and the Files API all came out of beta at once. Production, no beta header, available across the Claude model line.

What it actually does: a Skill is a versioned folder. Instructions, scripts, templates. It lives in Anthropic's sandbox and loads on demand, so you stop pasting your process into a chat window and start referencing it. The Browser Use tool reads a page's structure instead of its pixels, so it targets the real field instead of guessing at coordinates.

Why builders should care: we showed this exact shape on Tech Thursday. Our content engine doesn't get prompted image by image. A program we built with GitHub Copilot writes one long instruction covering six images, aspect ratios and every detail, then hands back a named, organized zip. That's a skill. Anthropic just made it a first-class object you don't have to host yourself.

Try this this week: take the prompt you retype the most. Write it once as a folder instead. The instructions, one finished example, and the three rules it keeps breaking. Load it as a skill and stop pasting.

The bigger signal: the unit of AI work is moving from the prompt to the package. Prompts are disposable. Skills compound.

Save this for your AI stack.
